name: Bad Brains
label: SST
lede: Four D.C. jazz-fusion players heard the Ramones, outran everyone in town and got barred from the clubs, and the teenagers trailing them into basements and galleries went on to start Dischord.

eras.title: Mind Power hears the Ramones
eras.text: Four young Black musicians from the D.C. area were playing Return to Forever-style jazz fusion as Mind Power until a friend put punk records in front of them. Within two years they were the fastest band anyone in Washington had seen, and the kids who would build Dischord were in the room.

years.h: Sid McCray teaches a jazz-fusion band the Ramones
years.p: Mind Power's guitarists are Gary Miller ([[Dr. Know|1cacaa8e-ba7b-408e-be51-6cc36b496156]]) and Paul Hudson, the bassist is [[Darryl Jenifer|f82bc155-c490-4b5f-bc5c-8462ecbdef01]], and the drummer is Paul's brother [[Earl Hudson|529a7b1b-f7bd-4c09-9f03-2227ab779a61]]. Their punk education comes from singer [[Sid McCray|2bae3f10-4b39-46af-ab76-6e0defc73989]].
years.xp:
Mind Power modeled itself on Return to Forever and the Mahavishnu Orchestra. According to Wikipedia, its first concert took place in the Hudsons' basement.

McCray, from a military family that had moved to Washington in 1968, sang with them first. Paul Hudson moved from guitar to the microphone as H.R. and McCray stepped aside, though McCray kept riding along on tours.

years.h: Mind Power renames itself after a Ramones song
years.p: The name comes from Bad Brain on the Ramones' Road to Ruin. The creed comes from Napoleon Hill's Think and Grow Rich: PMA, positive mental attitude.

years.h: Six songs in about an hour at Inner Ear
years.p: Bad Brains show up late to [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]]'s studio in Arlington and cut Pay to Cum, Black Dots and four more. Tape traders pass the session around for decades.

years.h: A Washington Post photographer follows H.R. to the next show
years.p: Lucian Perkins stumbles onto Bad Brains at Valley Green, a housing complex in Southeast D.C. H.R. tells him where they play next, and Perkins spends the fall shooting the scene.
years.xp:
Perkins photographed Bad Brains at Valley Green on September 9, at the Hard Art gallery on September 15 and twice at the Madam's Organ artists' cooperative, including November 11. The pictures became the book Hard Art DC 1979.

[[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]], then 14 or 15, was in those crowds. He has said Perkins was lucky to meet H.R. first, because H.R. pointed him to everything that followed.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bad Brains · Wikipedia: Bad Brains (album)
years.h: D.C. clubs shut the door on Bad Brains
years.p: Owners blacklist the band after its shows draw destructive crowds. Bad Brains answer with a song called Banned in D.C.
years.xp: The date is unsettled. Wikipedia's band page puts the ban in 1979; its page for the debut album says Bad Brains were barred from D.C.'s major clubs in 1981, just before they moved to New York.

eras.title: Shut out, then gone
eras.text: Locked out of the clubs, Bad Brains played galleries, basements and group houses, and the teenagers who opened for them became Minor Threat, SOA and the first Dischord roster. Then the band left for New York, and D.C. had to get along without its best band.

yt: Central Park, Rock Against Racism, May 3, 1980
years.h: Pay to Cum, 93 seconds on Bad Brain Records
years.p: Recorded in December 1979 at Dots Studio in New York with Jimi Quidd, the debut single (BB 001) has Stay Close to Me on the other side.
years.xp: Jenifer says he wrote Pay to Cum as a takeoff on the Ramones, and that it started out slower and kept speeding up. Filter later called it one of the fastest, most furious songs ever recorded.

years.h: The Teen Idles chase Bad Brains until they get a slot
years.p: Too young for most clubs, the Teen Idles follow the band around town and land an opening spot at Madam's Organ, an art gallery in a row house in Adams Morgan.
years.xp: Dischord's account of 1980 calls Bad Brains maybe the greatest band in the world. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]] had started playing punk after seeing a Bad Brains show, first in a band called the Slinkees.

years.h: Minor Threat's first show is a basement bill with Bad Brains
years.p: [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Jeff Nelson|51f7994c-949d-4dbe-89eb-2c33f42a5620]]'s new band plays to fifty people, opening for Bad Brains, [[Untouchables|16d88df0-a2a9-4b3b-87ff-84e90e312d40]], Black Market Baby and [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]]. Every band on the bill is from D.C.
years.xp: By then Wikipedia says the Teen Idles had about a hundred fans and ranked second in the scene only to Bad Brains. [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]], MacKaye's childhood friend and soon the singer of [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]], grew up on both bands.

years.big: "When Bad Brains moved to New York, the rest of us were pretty heartbroken."
years.h: Bad Brains move to New York
years.p: Alec MacKaye of Faith on the band that took the D.C. scene's best show to CBGB and stayed there.
years.xp:
In New York they fell in with Jerry Williams and his 171-A Studios in Alphabet City, where they recorded through the spring and fall of 1981. Their shows became the model for what New York hardcore would sound like.

Back home the kids they'd inspired were left to run the scene themselves.

years.cap: Dr. Know and H.R. in New York, 1981
years.h: Faith, a few weeks old, opens for Bad Brains at CBGB
years.p: Alec MacKaye's new D.C. band is on the CBGB stage that December, supporting Bad Brains. The set later comes out as Live at CBGB's.

eras.title: A cassette sets the speed limit
eras.text: The first album came out on cassette only, and it still sets the speed limit for hardcore. By then the band had turned to Rastafari, which produced the reggae interludes fans love and the ugliest episode in its history.

years.h: The ROIR "yellow tape"
years.p: Released only on cassette, the debut puts hardcore at impossible speed next to reggae. The cover shows the U.S. Capitol struck by lightning.
years.xp: Jay Dublee produced it from sessions at 171-A in May and August to October 1981; three tracks come from Jerry Williams' live tape. The cover art was by Donna Lee Parsons of Ratcage Records. The Decibel Hall of Fame inducted it in 2007.

years.h: H.R. learns Randy Biscuit Turner is gay, and Bad Brains leave a note
years.p: In Austin during the Rock Against Reagan tour, H.R. finds out the Big Boys singer is gay. According to Wikipedia, the band skips town without repaying a loan from Big Boys and leaves an antigay slur in a note.
years.xp:
The tour put Bad Brains on bills with [[MDC|0f3c4d10-e541-46f0-a589-61ad701c6ce4]] and Big Boys. H.R. and MDC's Dave Dictor had an intense confrontation over Turner before Bad Brains pulled out.

Both Austin bands wrote songs about it: Big Boys' Brickwall and MDC's Pay to Come Along, a jab at Bad Brains' own single.

years.cap: Darryl Jenifer and H.R. at the 9:30 Club, Washington, April 1983
years.h: Ric Ocasek of the Cars produces Rock for Light
years.p: The second album revisits songs from the yellow tape with a bigger sound.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists it as a ROIR release, one year after the self-titled cassette.

years.h: Pay to Cum turns up in Scorsese's After Hours
years.p: Martin Scorsese's New York night-crawl comedy uses the single. In 2006 it opens the documentary American Hardcore.

eras.title: The singer on the prison phone
eras.text: On Greg Ginn's SST, Bad Brains made the record that pulled metal and funk into their sound and became their best seller. Its singer cut part of it from a prison phone, and within months the Hudson brothers walked out for reggae.

years.h: I Against I is finished with H.R. on a prison phone
years.p: Bad Brains' SST debut blends hardcore with metal and funk. H.R. is locked up on a marijuana distribution charge, so he sings Sacred Love from Lorton Reformatory.
years.xp:
Ron Saint Germain produced it at Long View Farm, and recording the Sacred Love vocal down a prison phone line was his idea. Paul Rachman directed the video for the title track.

Wikipedia calls I Against I the band's best-selling album. Alternative Press put it at No. 9 in its top 99 of 1985 to 1995, and in 2019 Bad Brains re-recorded the title track with rapper Denzel Curry.

years.h: The Hudson brothers quit for reggae
years.p: H.R. and Earl Hudson walk out, so Dr. Know and Jenifer finish the tour with singer Taj Singleton and drummer Mackie Jayson, late of the [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]].

years.cap: Ticket stub for Bad Brains at the Masonic Prince Hall, St. Louis, August 24, 1989
years.h: H.R. comes back and sings over Taj Singleton's Quickness
years.p: Recording for Caroline starts in 1988 with Singleton; then the Hudsons return and H.R. replaces his vocals and lyrics. It's now counted as an early groove metal record.
years.xp: [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]] and [[Leeway|121193a5-cb8b-4182-968c-8ba607856fa2]] supported Bad Brains on the Quickness tour, including two weeks on the West Coast.

eras.title: Singers come and go, labels come calling
eras.text: The Hudsons left and returned twice more, the lead singer changed three times, and Bad Brains took major-label money from Epic and then Madonna's Maverick. The last reunion of the decade ended in violence and a jail cell.

years.h: Chuck Mosley of Faith No More takes the mic
years.p: The Hudsons quit again after the Quickness tour. Mackie Jayson returns on drums, and [[Chuck Mosley|9d2e1cba-9440-452f-bd00-999ecf1eb030]] sings nearly 60 shows in the U.S. and Europe.

years.h: Bad Brains and Henry Rollins cover Kick Out the Jams
years.p: The D.C. expatriates reunite with Rollins for the MC5 song on the Pump Up the Volume soundtrack.

years.h: Singer number four is born Dexter Pinto
years.p: Mosley leaves in January 1992. Israel Joseph I steps in, and Epic Records comes to Dr. Know with the band's first major-label deal.

years.cap: Bad Brains with Israel Joseph I in a promo shot from the Rise sessions, 1993
years.h: Rise, the one Epic album
years.p: Israel Joseph I sings. Mackie Jayson leaves mid-tour, and Philadelphia skater and musician [[Chuck Treece|ef661f53-d4b4-4903-811c-f3dcb1b970f3]] fills in on drums.

years.h: Madonna's Maverick puts out God of Love
years.p: H.R. and Earl Hudson are back. Bad Brains open for the [[Beastie Boys|9beb62b2-88db-4cea-801e-162cd344ee53]] on the Ill Communication tour and headline a U.S. run with a then-unknown [[Deftones|7527f6c2-d762-4b88-b5e2-9244f1e34c46]].

years.h: H.R. hits two fans with a mic stand in Kansas
years.p: Rolling Stone reports H.R. was arrested after striking two fans with a microphone stand. Wikipedia says there were violent incidents against the band's manager, fans and venue staff; H.R. went to jail and the band broke up.

eras.title: A new name, a Beastie at the board
eras.text: Bad Brains kept returning in pieces: old tapes, a name they could use, and finally a new album produced by one of the Beastie Boys, a band that grew up worshipping them. The original four played CBGB again before it closed.

years.h: Black Dots brings out the 1979 D.C. tapes
years.p: Caroline releases Bad Brains' earliest recordings, made in Washington in 1979, seventeen years after the fact.

years.h: The original four tour as Soul Brains
years.p: From 1998 to 2001, H.R., Dr. Know, Jenifer and Earl Hudson play under that name and release a live album. A year earlier they had remastered early tapes as The Omega Sessions.

years.h: CBGB gets one more Bad Brains show before it closes
years.p: The band plays its first shows in years at the Bowery club it had helped make, in the club's last year.

years.cap: Bad Brains at Slim's, San Francisco, September 24, 2007
years.h: Adam Yauch produces Build a Nation
years.p: The first studio album in a decade is produced by [[Adam Yauch|0d3bf21a-5eec-443c-9a37-b305598b0840]], MCA of the Beastie Boys. Israel Joseph I fills in for H.R. on some dates of the tour.
years.xp: [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]] has said he learned to drum by arranging pillows on his bed like a kit and playing along to Bad Brains.

years.h: Into the Future closes with MCA Dub
years.p: The ninth studio album ends with a tribute to Adam Yauch, who had produced Build a Nation and died that May. Jamie Saft joins on keyboards for touring.

eras.title: Tapes from the vault, news from the hospital
eras.text: Since 2016 the headlines have been medical and mournful: H.R.'s SUNCT, a Hall of Fame nomination that went nowhere, two former singers dead. Then, from a tape vault in Arlington, the session where it all started.

years.h: H.R. says he has SUNCT
years.p: He announces the rare disorder, which causes stabbing headaches, and a GoFundMe pays for treatment. Rolling Stone later reports surgery in 2017 that helped for a while.
years.xp:
In 2015 Bad Brains recorded the live EP The Woodstock Sessions with Jamaican singer Jesse Royal in H.R.'s place.

Benefit shows at the Teragram Ballroom in Los Angeles (December 2023) and Brooklyn Bowl in New York (April 2024) raised money for his medical bills.

years.h: Nominated for the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, not inducted
years.p: In December, Dr. Know and Jenifer tell Rolling Stone they hope to make an album called Mind Power.

years.h: Sid McCray sings with Bad Brains for the first time in 39 years
years.p: He joins them on The Regulator at a show that also features [[Lamb of God|298909e4-ebcb-47b8-95e9-cc53b087fc65]]'s Randy Blythe. Bad Brains haven't played live since.

years.h: Chuck Mosley dies in Cleveland at 57
years.p: Mosley, who fronted Bad Brains in 1990 and 1991, died at his home. His family said he died of the disease of addiction after a long period of sobriety.

years.h: Sid McCray dies
years.p: Bad Brains announce the death of the singer who turned them on to punk in a Facebook post three days later. No cause was reported.

years.h: Ian MacKaye mixes the 1979 Inner Ear tape
years.p: Trust Records releases Are You Ready: The First Studio Recording (Inner Ear, March 1979), the Arlington session tape traders have passed around for decades.
years.xp:
The six songs are Pay to Cum, Don't Bother Me, Black Dots, Migraine, Send No Flowers and Jamming at the Atlantis. Pete Lyman mastered it at Infrasonic.

Jenifer says the band's goal on stage was precision, like a finely tuned NFL team.
